# R369 v2 — corrected decode packed working-set arithmetic
Date: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Tokyo). Read-only arithmetic correction to R369 v1. No tests, builds, imports/AST/lint, GPU, profiler, process/service query, reset, Git operation, source edit, measurement, or v1 edit was performed. Main retains test/GPU ownership.

## Exact metadata identity and audited sum

Pack metadata read: `/home/yayoi/.local/share/strata-sycl/packs/qwen3.8-flash-next-iq3_s/native_experts.txt`. Its header identifies `# strata native experts v3`, 512 experts, declared total 50,292,326,400 bytes, and the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_S GGUF shard. The file has rows 0 through 47, with `blob_bytes` in column five. Summing that column over all 48 layers gives **98,227,200 bytes (93.676758 MiB) for one expert's blob at every layer**. Multiplying by the header's 512 experts gives exactly the declared total: 50,292,326,400 bytes.

The route is top K=10. Therefore, for one token selecting ten distinct experts at each of the 48 layers, the corresponding complete routed packed set is **982,272,000 bytes (936.767578 MiB; 982.272 MB decimal)**, assuming no expert is resident and each selected expert blob must be sourced once. There are 480 routed layer/expert entries. This is a logical packed-source extent total, not a measurement of physical RAM reads, DRAM traffic, memory-controller bandwidth, or H2D traffic.

For W tokens considered together, each layer's union can contain 10 to min(10W, 512) experts. Since the blob size is constant within a layer and the 48-layer one-expert sum is 98,227,200 B, the all-layer logical union bounds are:

| Window W | Packed union bytes, minimum to maximum | Minimum amortized per token | Maximum amortized per token |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | 982,272,000–1,964,544,000 B (936.77–1,873.54 MiB) | 491,136,000 B (468.38 MiB) | 982,272,000 B (936.77 MiB) |
| 4 | 982,272,000–3,929,088,000 B (936.77–3,747.07 MiB) | 245,568,000 B (234.19 MiB) | 982,272,000 B (936.77 MiB) |
| 8 | 982,272,000–7,858,176,000 B (936.77–7,494.14 MiB) | 122,784,000 B (117.10 MiB) | 982,272,000 B (936.77 MiB) |

Minimum means every token in the window selects the same ten experts at each layer; maximum means all routed IDs are distinct within each layer. These are set-union limits, not observations. The current no-MTP decode route uses one token per dispatch; these multi-token bounds describe hypothetical/verify-window reuse only. No current window overlap has been measured.

At a purely illustrative 70 tokens/s, the corrected no-resident logical source-extent rate is 68.75904 GB/s decimal (64.04 GiB/s). This is only the product of the packed-set accounting and the illustrative token rate. It must not be compared to a DDR theoretical rate as proof of feasibility or impossibility, because unique logical blobs do not establish physical DRAM traffic and no current sustained-DDR receipt was acquired.

## Correction to v1 interpretation

V1 incorrectly called the 48-row sum itself a per-token top-10 set and then reported 936.77 MiB/token. The 48-row sum represents **one expert per layer**. Top K=10 multiplies it by ten, so the correct one-token top-10 logical set is 982,272,000 B or 936.77 MiB. This fixes the working-set scale by a factor of ten relative to v1's reported 98,227,200 B/19.516 MiB figure. The earlier v1 window bounds and amortized values were consequently also ten times too small. V1 remains unchanged for audit history; this v2 supersedes its arithmetic and all conclusions that depended on that scale.

The source-design recommendations and limitations in v1 do not change: bounded request-scoped route-union counters and per-layer byte-weighted LRU simulations can estimate overlap/residency from actual IDs without traces or GPU synchronization, but neither establishes actual RAM traffic or critical-path savings. A static top-19 cache or dynamic reuse may help if measured routing supports it; actual route history, byte-weighted hit rate, CPU service savings, physical memory traffic, and full request speed remain unknown. Do not infer 70 tok/s feasibility either way from this arithmetic.

## Arithmetic provenance

- `native_experts.txt` header: native format version v3, `n_expert 512`, `total 50292326400`.
- The 48 blob-size entries (column five) sum to 98,227,200 B, one expert over all 48 layers.
- 98,227,200 × 512 = 50,292,326,400 B, matching the header exactly.
- 98,227,200 × 10 = 982,272,000 B, one token's top-10 set if all ten selected experts need a source blob at each layer.
- Window upper bound multiplies the top-10 set by W; lower bound is the top-10 set once. Per-token amortized bounds divide the union bounds by W.

No current request route histogram, route overlap, cache hit rate, sustained DDR measurement, physical DRAM traffic, or cache-on speedup was observed. This report corrects arithmetic only; no source or v1 report was changed.
